newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX tumbles below 3,000 pts after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX tumbles below 3,000 pts after Dow fall.

text.p: German shares fell sharply at the start of bourse trade on Friday in sympathy with Wall Street's overnight tumble, but dealers said this was not the large-scale correction many have been waiting for.

The DAX-30 index dropped 36.32 points to 2,997.14 in early trade as a wave programme-selling dragged the Dow to a sharply lower close. March DAX futures lost 39.5 points to 3,008.5, still above the psychological 3,000-point level.
Wall Street had finished lower on a wave of "programme" selling, where computers have been programmed to initiate sell orders once a certain set of conditions have been fulfilled.
"This is not a catastrophe," said one dealer. "It's being seen by some as an opportunity to buy," she noted, adding that it was likely the index would now remain within a tight range.

Another dealer confirmed that even despite the fact that it was a Friday, where market players are traditionally not keen to take significant new positions in the market, there was little chance of the losses being extended -- at least until Wall Street's open later today.
"Fundamentally, there is nothing wrong with the market and the currency situation is still positive," he said.
The dollar traded at 1.610 marks, still firm if slightly down on earlier levels.
German bund futures however were lower, in tune with a drop in U.S. Treasuries.

Shares in industrial giant Daimler-Benz slipped 1.35 marks to 114.70, in line with the market fall, despite a newspaper report that it saw sales rising to around 130 billion marks by the year 2000 from a current 106 billion.
Chief financial officer Manfred Gentz also said in an interview with the Handeslblatt newspaper he did not expect the group to seek to raise any capital this year.
